body: Only `planRound` is guarded before `beginRun`; failures in the subsequent `noteAttempt` writes can reject this function after the run record and `running` results have already been created. The message handler then returns the generic refusal, but no task is launched or settled and the stale run blocks later starts until cleanup. Post-`beginRun` setup failures need to settle the started run (or otherwise roll it back) before returning a refusal.

If the `recordResult` storage write rejects, neither `stopSearches()` nor `endRun()` is reached. The caller's error handler then calls `finishSearch` again, which can fail at the same write, leaving the result running, the run record present, and alarms/badges active—the failure mode this teardown is intended to prevent. Cleanup should be best-effort/finally-protected so a transient result-write error cannot strand the round.

The run-id guard protects `recordResult` and `endRun`, but `stopSearches()` clears the global search badge, short timer, and every `openTabAlarm:*` alarm without checking the run id. A late callback from an ended round can therefore enter this function after a new round starts; its guarded result write is ignored, then it clears the new round's alarms and can stall that round. Scope cleanup to `runId` or re-check that this run is still current before performing the global cleanup.

The tab can run the content script before this `await noteSearchTab(...)` completes: `tabs.create()` starts page loading immediately, while `openAndClose` first awaits tracking and another `stillRunning` check. In that window the script's first `bingFirstResult` request sees no matching `searchTabIds`, is refused, and `oncePerPageRun` prevents a later request, so enabled first-result navigation is skipped nondeterministically. Record the tab id before any post-creation await (or otherwise make the authorization visible before the content script can ask).

### Attempt failure leaves search flag **Medium Severity** When `noteAttempt` fails after `beginRun`, the new catch settles results and ends the run record but never clears search progress. `beginRun` has already set `isSearching` on `taskProgress`, and neither `settleUnresolved` nor `endRun` turns that flag off.
